consumer: The frontend asking a yes/no possession question 'is the player currently holding a 1st_aid?', the same question an engine possession check (Character::has_amount / has_item_with family) answers.
scope: A full possession check over everything the player has on their person, recursing into worn/held container contents and nested pockets — the engine's has_amount-family reach, not just top-level item stacks.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items dumps raw wielded_items()/worn/inv_const_slice() lists into JSON; it enumerates top-level item containers (simulation state S) and asks the consumer to re-derive the possession verdict rather than returning the engine-computed predicate's result.
divergence: A 1st_aid stored inside a worn backpack or nested container pocket: the engine's possession check counts it as held, but the flat top-level wielded/worn/inventory walk in write_carried_items misses it, so the frontend's re-derived answer says 'not holding' while the engine predicate says 'holding'.
